entry.text: Your first shift where nobody should come in wanting to discuss the bloody organ, confess what they did to it, or explain why technically it wasn't their fault.
Things were still a little heated after Mass yesterday, but I think the town's finally exhausted itself.
Now, as for another duty that had absolutely nothing to do with running a tobacconist...

tooth.text: Looks like the tooth found its way into the right hands?
Good. Till looks a bit lonely without it, though.

tooth_toothShift7.text: No need to worry about the tooth anymore. I figured it out. Turns out it wasn't actually that difficult.

decor_decorLateorder.text: Also, been meaning to ask about that thing you hung up over there.

decor2_outOfBin.text: Did you loot that out of some fairground rubbish heap?

decor2_badTaste.text: It's... atrocious. Cheerful. And hurting the eyes in a very festive way.

decor2_uglyHome.text: Well. That's got... just the right kind of domestic ugliness to it, I must say.

decor3.text: I like it. Really suits the shop.

decor_decorShift7.text: Also, a parcel showed up yesterday. I didn't order anything, so I assume this is your doing.
No idea who your mysterious "trusted supplier" of interior decorations is, but... ehm.
Good choice. It suits the place.

pay.text: ...Ah, right. Before I forget... here. Your pay.
Thought it was going against the debt.
There was a debt.... Technically. Some bits and pieces, here and there.
But nowhere near enough to justify making you stand here twice a week for this long.
You looked like you needed somewhere to be.
Anyway, we're square. If you show up Friday, it'll be because you made a poor personal choice. Which I fully support.

entry.text: Oh, look. The entire music department.
And the tobacconist seems to have assembled its full workforce too. Remarkable.
Over tobacco and papers for me, please.
Oh, and... um, Menthol Morleys too.
Oh-ho. How very attentive of you, sunshine.

response.text: Wonderfully dull again. Bad pianos, bad clarinets, one very bad accordion. No organ guts spread across every available surface, finally.
Yeah. It was nice to actually play it again yesterday instead of stepping over bits of it in the workshop.
It was... actually not as bad as I expected.
Meh. Would've been better if Gail hadn't cheated at cards.
You say the same thing about my wife every time you lose to her.
Because she cheats every time I lose.
Mm. Poor Félix. Outwitted by women yet again.
Very well. We've... expanded the treatment.
Turns out it works much better when you set fire to it first.

options.text: What am I getting you two again?

response.text: Bruyère for our elderly ex-smoker. Over, papers and a mysterious packet of Menthol Morleys for our Romeo.

organ_someoneSolved.text: Mhm. Parish scraped together enough to repair the important bits, and yesterday it successfully performed its basic duties as an organ.
Um... It did make that grotesque honk during the last hymn. I don't remember it doing that before.
Well, good as new was never an option. At this point, best we can do is keep frankensteining it together whenever another bit gives up.

organ2_organComplete.text: But maybe we could finally get the old Vox Humana working again?
Mm. Suppose we can afford it now. Though God knows why you'd want that miserable whine back.

organ2.text: But no one here ever minded its crooked charm. I think it'll be fine.

organ.text: Even if it was probably the last time we heard it there.
Well... We did what we could. Even got it through Mass. Almost.

Halfway through, half the organ had already dismantled itself under my hands. Whatever was still attached kept sticking, wheezing or doing something else it wasn't supposed to. I don't know how we reached the end.
At least it said its goodbye.
For a moment I thought it might take me with it.
There, there. First the Menthol Morleys, then you may perish tragically.

wrong_items.text: Big list, I know. Four whole things.

wrong_price.text: Mm. Nasty one, isn't it? All those numbers.

checkout.text: Thanks. Right, back to the workshop.
I'll come by in a bit.
Don't take all day. That accordion's waiting, and I'd rather we suffered together.
Right, I think I'll head out too. Kid, shop's yours.
